correctness.rationale: Termwise horizontal integration yields exact (T_gf)_m=(log m)^-1 sum_{k|m,k>=2} b_k log k a_{m/k}, so T_g= D M_h, h=-g', D diagonal 1/log m (m>=2), compact and s_n(D)=1/log(n+1). The Hardy polydisk Bohr lift gives ||M_h||=sup_{t}|g'(it)| using rationally independent prime logarithms and finite prime-smooth polynomial approximants to the multiplier norm. The ideal inequality gives a sharp upper K/log n. For each finite prime-smooth near-maximizer F, shifts by P-coprime m in a dyadic range give mutually orthonormal domain vectors and orthogonal images supported on disjoint arithmetic fibers; inclusion–exclusion supplies positive-density many m, and the Courant–Fischer min–max bound gives lower (K-eps)/log(C n). Sending eps down proves the limit; logarithmic counting inversion and no-Schatten follow. For g=2^-s+4^-s-8^-s, |h(z)|²/(log2)²=20-8cos(theta)-12cos²(theta) has peak 64/3 at cos=-1/3. Independent coefficient/multiplier tests and 2049 sampled circle values corroborate this.

originality.rationale: Brevig–Perfekt–Seip 2016 arXiv:1602.04729, Section 7 (page 34), was inspected in full PDF and explicitly proves polynomial-symbol compactness and Theorem 7.2 non-Schatten membership for EVERY nonconstant symbol. These qualitative deductions are therefore not novel. The new sharp limit has the quantitatively determined constant ||g'||∞ and exponential singular counting function; the cited theorem only lower bounds column norms by one nonzero coefficient. Weighted Dirichlet Bergman and BMOA studies address other ambient spaces and do not give the H² exact leading coefficient. Resultary returned finite Cesàro and Hardy–Volterra spectra unrelated to the arithmetic fiber asymptotic. Broad compact Toeplitz multiplier singular-value laws remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: A more general compact diagonal-times-polynomial-multiplier spectral asymptotic theorem could imply this formula under an arithmetic-fiber identification.
